title: Discovery: cost economics and deployment options - Peregrine Tech
summary: Initial discovery focused on cost/unit economics across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options. Peregrine is evaluating per-token hosted pricing vs reserved dedicated capacity and an eventual private deployment for data residency. Key items: current volumes, budget targets, expected latency SLOs, and feasibility of batching/caching to reduce per-token cost. AE to share pricing spreadsheet and SE to run a small benchmark using Peregrine sample traces.
topics: Current infra and average token volumes
Per-token hosted pricing vs Dedicated reserved capacity
Batching and KV/prefix caching impact on effective unit cost
action_items: Sofia Martinez: Share detailed pricing spreadsheet and example unit economics (hosted vs dedicated) - due 2026-01-20
Ethan Cole (SE): Run benchmark with Peregrine sample prompts to show batching and KV cache savings; share results - due 2026-01-24
Asha Kapoor (Customer): Provide 7-day traffic trace and representative prompt set (anonymized) - due 2026-01-22
Janelle Park (Procurement): Send list of required contractual clauses for Private deployment - due 2026-01-30
next_steps: Send pricing deck + hosted vs dedicated cost model
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-run) next week
Provision trial hosted account and sample API keys
Agree pilot success metrics (cost per 1M tokens, p95 latency, error rate)
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-01-17
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 60m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Asha Kapoor (Peregrine Head of ML), Tom Rives (Peregrine CTO), Liam Chen (Peregrine SRE), Janelle Park (Peregrine Procurement)
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia with Redwood Inference, this is Ethan our SE. Quick intro?
[00:08] Asha Kapoor: Hi, I'm Asha, Head of ML at Peregrine, we run a hybrid pipeline for customer insights, lots of real-time prompts.
[00:15] Tom Rives: Tom here, CTO, I'm mostly interested in cost and compliance.
[00:20] Ethan Cole: Cool, thanks. Today we'll focus on cost per unit economics and deployment options dashboard d--- hosted, dedicated, private and how batching/caching moves the needle.
[00:30] Sofia Martinez: Quick agenda: get your current volume, budget, topology; walk pricing; talk batching/K V cache impacts; next steps.
[00:42] Liam Chen: We're seeing about 120M tokens a month today, spikes to 200M on marketing days, p95 latency target ~350ms. Budget: we want to keep infra under $25k/mo initially.
[01:00] Sofia Martinez: OK got it, so that 120 to 200M range. Are these tokens mostly generation or embeddings?
[01:06] Asha Kapoor: Mostly generation, some embeddings for search indexes but small fraction.
[01:11] Ethan Cole: For hosted, our typical per-token tiers for the models you saw in the deck run around $0.0008 to $0.0025 per token for larger context models -- sorry those numbers are examples, we'll send exact tiers -- but important is effective cost after batching and prefix/K V cache.
[01:32] Tom Rives: Wait, can you repeat the ranges, I missed the higher end?
[01:36] Ethan Cole: Yeah, roughly eight tenths of a mil to two and a half mil per token -- I said that terribly -- basically $0.0008 to $0.0025 per token depending on model.
[01:46] Asha Kapoor: That seems high, does batching reduce that a lot?
[01:50] Ethan Cole: Yes. Example: if you have repeated prefixes or you can batch multiple short requests in 1 inference step, you can see 20-60% effective token reduction. For us batching is continuous batching in the runtime so it groups requests on the GPU microsecond-level.
[02:08] Sofia Martinez: Also prefix/K V cache reduces generation tokens when you reuse conversation or system prompts; we've seen customers go from 120M billed tokens to an effective 50-70M depending on reuse.
[02:20] Tom Rives: How does dedicated reserved capacity pricing compare if we commit monthly?
[02:24] Sofia Martinez: Dedicated is a commit model -- you pay for reserved GPU pools; unit economics depend on utilization. For heavy, steady loads like 120-200M tokens, dedicated often beats hosted after you hit a certain utilization because your amortized GPU cost per token drops. But you take on operational lead time and minimum commit.
[02:41] Ethan Cole: To give a concrete example: a 4-GPU dedicated pool for your workload might cost X per hour -- (note: we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet). At 70-80% utilization the per-token cost can be 30-50% lower than hosted. But at 20-30% utilization hosted can be cheaper.
[03:01] Asha Kapoor: What about private/VPC deployment? We have data residency needs and SOC2 plus encrypted keys with our K M S.
[03:07] Sofia Martinez: Private is available as a VPC or on-prem option. It adds platform licensing and infra; we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption. It's more expensive upfront but necessary for regulated data; we can show TCO over 12-24 months.
[03:22] Tom Rives: We need audit logs and SSO -- SAML, RBAC. Does Redwood provide those for Private?
[03:27] Ethan Cole: Yes, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs are included in Private plus Dedicated higher tiers. Hosted has SOC2 and standard enterprise controls.
[03:36] Liam Chen: Back to cost -- can you show us effective cost per 1M tokens after caching/batching so we can compare to our $25k budget?
[03:42] Sofia Martinez: Absolutely. Quick mental math: if hosted list is say $0.0012/token and you get 40% effective reduction via batching/cache, your effective cost becomes ~$0.00072/token. For 120M tokens that's about $86k -- which is above $25k, so that indicates you either need stronger caching, a smaller model, or dedicated reserved capacity.
[04:04] Asha Kapoor: That makes sense. We're willing to trade some latency for cheaper ops but need p95 under 400ms.
[04:10] Ethan Cole: That's doable with Dedicated and correct batching config; we can tune batch windows to balance latency vs throughput. Also quantized models or smaller variants reduce token compute cost.
[04:22] Tom Rives: Any typical numbers for quantization impact? Like int8 vs fp16?
[04:26] Ethan Cole: Int8 can reduce GPU memory and improve throughput; compute efficiency often goes up 1.5-2x depending on kernel maturity. That roughly halves GPU time per token in some cases, but accuracy/regression risks exist -- we'll show model-specific tradeoffs.
[04:41] Sofia Martinez: Also routing policies -- you can route low-latency requests to more expensive models and background tasks to cheaper variants. That helps cost targeting.
[04:50] Asha Kapoor: Regarding batching, what's the typical batching window? We have many short prompts from mobile clients.
[04:55] Ethan Cole: Our runtime uses continuous batching that groups sub-100ms arrivals; effective window is dynamic. For mobile short prompts you still get batching benefit if arrival rate is enough. We'll validate with your traffic trace.
[05:08] Janelle Park: Procurement question -- for dedicated reserved capacity what contract lengths and penalties?
[05:13] Sofia Martinez: Typical is 12- or 24-month commits; we can do monthly but price protection favors annual. Penalties are negotiable based on enterprise terms; we'll surface standard SOW.
[05:22] Tom Rives: For pilot, can we do hosted with credits to validate caching numbers before committing?
[05:26] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we can provision a hosted trial env and run the SE benchmark; that usually addresses unit economics before a commit.
[05:33] Ethan Cole: I'll run the benchmark with your prompts and measure billed tokens with and without prefix cache enabled and measure p95 latency.
[05:41] Asha Kapoor: Great. Also want to know ops burden for Private, like how much maintenance our SREs need to run it on-prem.
[05:49] Ethan Cole: Private requires more SRE involvement but we offer an on-call runbook and optional managed services. We'll include an ops checklist.
[05:57] Sofia Martinez: Ok let's recap actions -- we'll send the pricing spreadsheet, set up trial, SE will run bench, Asha to share traffic and prompt sets. Anything else?
[06:07] Tom Rives: Can you include model regression monitoring and alerting costs? We have strict quality SLAs.
[06:12] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; that's an add-on, we'll include pricing.
[06:20] Liam Chen: One more quick thing -- caching: do you cache on a per-customer basis? We'll need isolation.
[06:25] Ethan Cole: Yes, cache shards are tenant-aware and respect data isolation; for Private we can keep cache inside your VPC.
[06:32] Janelle Park: Procurement will need a sample SOW and standard security questionnaire.
[06:35] Sofia Martinez: We'll attach the security pack and SOW template.
[06:40] Asha Kapoor: Great, thanks. That gives us a path forward.
[06:44] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everybody, we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the SE deep-dive.
[06:50] [Call ends]
